To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the use of contextual information in a caption improves the performance of a visual classifier, and ii) the performance of a name-face association system is not only dependent on its ability to detect faces in an image but also on its ability to extract contextual information from a caption.

1) the use of the text surrounding the image is important to achieve good performance, 2) the use of context is crucial to deal with the high level of noise present in FAN-Large and 3) the use of contextual information can be improved by using more sophisticated contextual features, such as those proposed in this paper.

(1) the state-of-the-art methods for face naming are not able to deal with the large noise present in the data; (2) the performance of the state-of-the art methods is not improved by the use of contextual features derived from captions, but (3) new features that we propose, based on the analysis of the captions, are able to significantly increase the accuracy of the methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to best use large scale Web image collections and their associated text captions for training classifiers of visual concepts.
the question of whether the Web can be used to train classifiers for the task of automatic face naming.
the problem of how to use the Web for training automatic classifiers that can be applied to new images of people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem is still far from solved and that there is a need for more research.
, while the problem of associating names to faces in images has been largely solved, the problem of associat-ing names to images has not, and remains an open problem.
none of the approaches we have tested is able to provide a satisfactory solution to the problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current methods are still far from being able to exploit all the information available in the captions, which are rich and complex.
, in spite of the large amount of noise in the dataset, the use of contextual features derived from captions can be very effective in the presence of a small amount of training data.
the best performance on FAN-Large is obtained by a simple baseline that exploits only the image and the text captions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FAN-Large is a very challenging dataset for automatic face naming.
the use of contextual features derived from captions can significantly improve the performance of existing approaches for face naming.
the use of contextual information from the caption is crucial for achieving high accuracy, but it is also the source of the largest errors.
